absent: Numeric encodings and widths of scheduling policies, priorities, clamp limits, and bandwidth units.
Locking and calling context for admission validation, policy classifiers, and fork initialization beyond stated runqueue and RCU requirements.
Behavior of referenced but unrouted helpers for clocks, cpufreq, priority inheritance, topology, and NUMA faults.
Timer expiry, throttle, and task work state machines beyond initial arming.
Error paths and concurrency guarantees for remote wakeup queuing and idle balancing.

findings.text: Per runqueue deadline bandwidth totals never remain negative in observable state. A subtraction that would wrap is clamped to zero and treated as a warning event, and the running total is expected not to exceed the overall total.
Deadline bandwidth decrement operations require the owning runqueue lock to be held by the caller.
Special deadline entities are excluded from running bandwidth accounting while ordinary entities decrement the running total by their bandwidth contribution.

Deadline admission accepts governor flagged requests unconditionally and otherwise requires nonzero deadline, sufficiently large runtime for fixed point precision, clear sign bit on deadline and period, ordered runtime deadline period with missing period defaulting to deadline, and period within configured minimum and maximum.
A deadline parameter change is defined as any difference in runtime, deadline, period, or masked deadline flags between the task entity and the requested attributes.

Policy classification treats normal and batch as fair with extended included when that class is configured, treats fifo and round robin as realtime, and treats idle, fair, realtime, and deadline as the valid set.

Static priority assignment gives deadline a fixed top value, derives realtime priority inversely from realtime level, and otherwise derives from niceness. Effective realtime priority is the minimum of the requested value and any priority inheritance donor when that mechanism is configured, otherwise the requested value unchanged.

Unprivileged scheduler changes are constrained by ownership and privilege escalation rules covering niceness reduction, realtime policy entry and priority increase within resource limit, blanket privilege requirement for deadline, exit from idle, same user identity, and preservation of reset on fork, with fallback to a nice capability check.

Utilization clamp requests are validated for range and ordering of minimum and maximum, reset to defaults on class change for non user values or on explicit negative sentinel with a distinct realtime minimum default, and enable the clamp mechanism on success.
When the clamp feature is not configured, validation reports unsupported and application is a no operation.

Moving a deadline boosted task to a lower class preserves inheritance by adopting the donor inheritance context and requesting replenishment at next enqueue. Without inheritance configuration this adjustment is absent.

Transition into the extended scheduling class is denied with access error when the feature is active and the target task is marked disallowed and changes policy, otherwise permitted. Without the class the check always permits.

Synchronous task function execution always holds the priority inheritance lock and additionally holds the runqueue lock when the task is running, waking, queued, or still on processor, using ordered state and queue membership observations with barriers.

Pending remote wakeups are drained on the local processor under lock with clock update, waiting for departure from processor and correcting processor assignment before activation. The pending indicator is cleared only after at least one activation to avoid false idle observation.

Wakeup and current task observation paths serialize against scheduling with runqueue locking. Idle wakeup also uses a read side critical section with double checked idle state, and snapshot uses barriers around current pointer access.
Average idle estimation ignores missing timestamps, otherwise blends the latest idle interval with one eighth weight and clamps the result to twice the worst balance cost before clearing the stamp.

Processor relationship queries report equal capacity when asymmetry is inactive or processors match or architectural capacities match, report shared resources on identity or equal share domain, and polling idle handling can suppress an interprocessor signal with a trace event.

New task scheduler state starts with cleared queue membership, zeroed fair execution and virtual time accounting, cleared deadline timing bandwidth and status flags with self inheritance, and reset realtime list timeout slice and queue flags.

Optional scheduler extensions initialize to neutral defaults including empty dispatch structures with invalid identifiers and default slice, reset cache work and group references, armed throttle work protected against double queue, and zeroed scan and fault accounting with thread versus address space handling for preferred node.
Deadline entity lifecycle begins with cleared tree linkage, two monotonic hard relative timers for active and inactive handling, and cleared parameters.

Nonuniform memory scan pacing derives window count from resident size and configured scan size, derives floor and scaled minimum and maximum periods, weights the maximum by group membership and shared versus private fault balance, and indexes fault counters by category, node, and privacy.
Wakeup and observation entry points expose waking by state mask, conditional reschedule of an idle processor, and locked snapshot of a processor current task.
Extended entity uses negative one to denote no assigned sticky, holding, or runnable processor.

Bandwidth accounting must tolerate decrement races by clamping rather than wrapping, and wakeup paths must handle tasks still on processor or with stale processor assignment without loss or false idle.
Synchronous task observation and wakeup helpers are available for cross processor use.
Parameter validation and policy classification helpers are available to admission and change paths.
Realtime bandwidth control is considered enabled when the configured realtime runtime limit is non negative.
Nonuniform memory balancing activity is gated by a static branch key that defaults to disabled.
